title: RPG Maker MV Project Series' Idea: Multi-Cross Sagas

posts.author: Pokejedservo
posts.body:
Multi-Cross Sagas RPG Maker MV idea.
Well folks after learning about some plugins for RPG Maker MV such as Yanfly’s Party System & Row Management System where you can add in additional party members up to 8 via 2 rows of 4. (Potentially more but that might cause technical difficulties.) I admit one of the reasons why I was not certain about working on a RPG Maker on PC even if they are normally more robust in features than the ones on Consoles. But while a project on RPG Maker MV can have 1000 playable characters overall you can only have 4 characters in your party. While granted hardly anyone would need 1000 characters usually but if you have a fairly high amount of playable characters then having 4 in a party at a time may seem a bit small & limiting. But thanks to plugins I can potentially do larger party sizes. Anyways just to get on with it here is my main idea here.
Basically take any given RPG game such as Final Fantasy 4, Final Fantasy 6, Final Fantasy 7, Dragon Quest 4, EarthBound and the like. And be able to add in Multiple versions based off of various companies such as Nintendo, Sega, Capcom, SNK, Square, Enix, Konami, Hudson and more. It's very much like the Multi-Crossover Fusion Fic idea I had for the SRPG studio in this DeviantArt Journal I did some time ago at…
https://www.deviantart.com/pokejedservo/journal/I-have-a-couple-of-ideas-for-SRPG-Studio-989808195
In which the characters from the base game will of course appear in their roles but the various characters from the franchises of that company “version” will also appear in various ways. Whether they be new allies for our heroes and/or the villains of the base game. Also in other ways such as new NPC roles (both Major & Minor) to replace the generic nameless NPCs such as townspeople, merchants, innkeepers and the like. And much like the 2nd idea in that aforementioned journal I am thinking of having the franchises be represented in 3 tiers.
Primary- Most of the Franchises that the Company owns (or in some cases is most directly tied with). Will most likely get prominent playable/enemy/NPC roles for sure. (Though as for NPCs I am referring to whether it be for story roles and/or staff members of the “Hub” world
in the game.) Each franchise that would be represented in this series will have at least one version that will be in the “Primary” tier for. (Though I am toying with the idea of some franchises getting two.)
[*]Secondary- Franchises whom the company doesn’t own (or no longer owns) but has a rather strong history with such as crossovers, adaptations and the like on a fairly regular basis. Some of the characters might get prominent playable/NPC roles, but there is a good chance they would get more secondary roles though.
[*]Minor- Franchises that have a small history with said company. (Published at least one game/comic, made a reference or two about said franchise in the past, loosely connected thanks to other corporations that the company is/was with). One or two characters might get a secondary playable role but will most likely be minor NPCs/Enemies. Some franchises might get little scenes from plays/books (and in games with more modern settings TV/Movies/Comics/Video Games) and be world building window dressing. Be forewarned that some depictions might not be favorable such as getting a satirical jab or that some of the characters may wind up as cannon fodder against one of the enemies. But in all fairness there is a fair chance that these franchises might get more than one depiction though. (Another forewarning that the justifications for some of these may be really loose but it will be mainly with franchises that have very few connections to begin with.)
So yes characters in one version may be prominent allies and/or foes in one version but be basically glorified cameos in another. Like I said before I did make sure that all franchises will have at least one franchise that they will be prominent in. So while I will make sure that all franchises will appear in more than one version one way or another but regrettably some franchises might only be remotely prominent in about one or two but I will try to keep that to a minimum. There will be various other little differences like how some Characters in the 2nd and 3rd tiers would also provide NPC Ally Soldiers in certain games but how they would normally fare…
2nd Tier- At best would be completely successful in their mission to at worst have some injured members but are otherwise safe.
3rd Tier- At best they would be highly injured but survive to at worst get slaughtered by the enemy with little to no survivors.
One other little difference is that while all the franchises would generally be depicted as the Franchise in general in Primary Tiers. But while this might happen in the 2nd and 3rd tiers as well but often enough often parts of the franchise would be depicted. Various franchises like Mega Man (Classic, X, Legends, Battle Network), Fire Emblem (Archanea Trilogy, Jugdral Duology, 3 Houses, etc.) and the like. For example while Fire Emblem Three Houses would of course be 1st Tier with the rest of the FE franchise with Nintendo. But 3 Houses/Hope would be 2nd Tier with Tecmo & Koei due to their connection as they were involved in the Fodlan FE games. Meanwhile thanks to Fire Emblem Warriors the earlier FE series’ such as Archanea would be in 2nd Tier to maybe 3rd.
Anyways the stories will be slightly to fairly altered (depending on which game we are talking about) as all the characters who are native to the game will be in all versions. But each version will give the playable cast a significant boost (mostly characters from the 1st Tier, a fair amount of characters from the 2nd Tier and maybe a few from the 3rd.) So in other words in any of these games the main hero won’t have to go alone at first. (Though how many allies might depend on how I can make the party sizes whether it be 8 [4X2 Rows], 10 [5X2 Rows] or 12 [6X2 Rows]. Though I have been told 8 via 4X2 is more likely to be feasible.) But the fact that our heroes will have additional allies can have some effect on the plot like for example in Earthbound, Buzz Buzz will have two allies from the future accompany him to aid Ness as they manage to save Buzz Buzz from his demise early in the game. (But more on that later.) However to the more traditionalist fans out there some of the ally additions won’t change things too much like Ragnar leading a group of soldiers from Burland early in Dragon Quest 4 rather than do it singlehandedly.
Now as for Villains the games will get a substantial amount of new subbosses though characters from the franchises on the 1st & 2nd tiers will more likely be related to the enemies from the game. (But not always.) Meanwhile characters from the 3rd tier (and in some cases the 1st two) will generally be more minor. But in each game I will add in various little submissions for our heroes to go to before they get to handle the more prominent foes. (But whether this would happen right away or at a certain point will also differ depending on the game.) Will the Big Bad of the game always remain so? Well in most cases yes but I am toying with the idea of having certain games be extended when a new villain usurps the game’s Big Bad and takes over extending the storyline here but of course who does so will differ on the version. One example would be for a RPG Maker version of the Konami NES classic “Adventures of Bayou Billy” where after Billy West and his new allies save Annabelle. Godfather Gordon, the game’s Big Bad, gets dispatched by his mysterious benefactor who will take over his operations in the Bayou. But I also have some other slightly less dynamic but still variable roles like in Earthbound who would be the “Mysterious Business Partner” that will help Aloysios and Pokey get rich with the Monotoli Building at Fourside for example. Though many villains that are version guests will of course stay villainous but there is a good chance that some of them will be allies from the start (or will become allies later) again this is highly variable.
While in games that have pre-established characters there will be plenty of new allies and who they are will depend on the version. But what of games that did not have named characters and are more based off of occupation such as the original Final Fantasy for example? In that case I am thinking of having a fair amount of the 1st Tier characters be in the game in which there will be plenty of male & female choices for Fighter, Thief, Black Belt, Black Mage, White Mage, Red Mage and Ninja. (Yes I am thinking of having Thief & Ninja be separate classes.) In which you can pick the party set-up you want and if you want you can keep the same characters throughout the game but if you want you can exchange them for others later. I am toying with the idea of certain games being a little mix of both such as Dragon Quest 3 (Keep the Hero & Heroine as siblings but most of the allies will vary. But I admit I am still trying to figure out the logistics there.) Due to the fact that each game will get a large amount of playable characters I will be thinking of giving each a certain “Hub” area where you can change your party members at will especially when you have more than enough. This may not be a problem at first since certain games like Final Fantasy 6 and Chrono Trigger did have Hub areas even if they didn’t happen until a little later on in their respective games. In certain games I may alter the plot a bit to give the game a hub a lot sooner, or at all for that matter. (Like for example remember when I said in Earthbound I will give Buzz Buzz two additional allies who will aid & save him? Well one of my other ideas is that said allies will take Ness to their ship they used for Time Travel that is implied to be hidden in the mountain that the Meteorite hit early in the game.) But in some games I am considering giving them more than one “Hub” area to potentially use.
While a fair amount of these games will most likely cover one game and one storyline. But some of these games might cover a duology (Dragon Quest 1 & 2) or a Trilogy (Fire Emblem Archanea) and the like. While these may seem rather overwhelming at first glance but if anything this might be beneficial as it can help make adding a large amount of characters be more manageable. But these games will still most likely be treated as standalone but some might be seen as a direct sequel/prequel to others since some stories might not be able to be held even in a “trilogy” but I will work around that if necessary. One might ask why give a game multiple versions as wouldn’t it be horribly overwhelming? It certainly seems that way for making one game. But if you want to make more than one game, if anything it actually seems like a fairly efficient way to make a series by mixing old & new assets. Now I’m sure there are cynics who would find making multiple versions of one game be highly overwhelming for any one person to do. And I admit I get that but I have learned that trying to suppress ideas you have does not help one’s creative process at all. In other words even if this is far too big for someone like me to do then maybe it will at least help me come up with something more manageable.
Now one last thing to speak of would be which companies I would be making “versions” with? There would be various examples such as the following…
(Video Game)
Nintendo, Sega, Capcom, SNK, Konami, Hudson, Square, Enix, Taito, Arc System Works, Technos, Namco, etc.
(TV/Movie)
Disney, Universal, 20th Century Fox, Paramount, Warner Bros., LucasFilm/Art, Hasbro, Mattel, etc.
(Comics)
Marvel, DC Comics, Archie, Dark Horse Comics
(American Animation)
Hanna Barbera, Bluth Studio, DiC/Wildbrain, Film Roman, etc.
(Japanese Animation)
TOEi Animation, TMS Entertainment, Madhouse, Bandai, Kadokawa, Ghibli, etc.
Though I am considering the idea of also adding in Anime English Dub companies such as Viz, ADV/Sentai, FUNimation/CrunchyRoll, Pioneer/Geneon and the like. Yes I am aware of the aforementioned Anime studio list but I also figured this would be a way to help ensure that certain anime shows done by lesser known studios might get a shot to be included. But I figured that if a company has more than one 1st, 2nd and 3rd Tier franchises then they have a good chance. While I admit that not every franchise they may have would be represented but many of them will. Rest assured I am aware that a fair amount of the companies I already mentioned are connected (Konami-Hudson, Square-Enix-Taito, Namco-Bandai, etc.) and some are formally connected (Disney-DiC) but I am using those to often build the 2nd and 3rd Tiers for the various versions. Will every franchise I’m covering in these versions get RPG/SRPG games of their own? To be honest most likely no. Oh sure there are some franchises that I am thinking of extending into a RPG Maker title (like the aforementioned Bayou Billy for example.) But a good portion of these franchises would if any game be more suited for things like Visual Novel Studios, OpenBOR, MUGEN, Pixel Game Maker and the like. (Though to be fair I have heard that RPG Maker projects can have Visual Novel elements.) Now one might ask why should I bother with these “versions” and just make a truly Multi-Cross game with any franchises I can think of? Well that may seem nice & simple on paper but it's been generally said that the maximum number of playable characters in programs like RPG Maker MV and the like is 1000 which would most likely exceed that. No such an idea could only possibly work in SRPG Studio where the character counts could be significantly higher could this be remotely feasible (and even then that might be a stretch.) So what do you folks think? Yes I admit this may not be the most realistic idea here but like I said before trying to suppress your ideas does nothing but harm your creative process. Could I find ways to make more manageable ideas? Perhaps but still what do you folks think?
